responsibility: This module provides GCC’s compiler-supplied public headers that expose language-standard and ABI-support interfaces directly from compiler builtins, predefined target macros, and runtime conventions, especially for freestanding or compiler-managed environments. Its files implement standard C and GNU compatibility headers such as the common type and limits family (<stddef.h>, <stdint.h>, <float.h>), source-language feature wrappers (<stdbool.h>, <stdalign.h>, <stdnoreturn.h>, <iso646.h>, <stdcountof.h>), varargs and atomic interfaces built on GCC builtins (<stdarg.h>, <stdatomic.h>, checked integer arithmetic), fixed-point and type-generic math support, and dispatch wrappers that choose between system and GCC-provided definitions when needed. It also includes target- or runtime-facing ABI headers such as ARM unwinding declarations, while obsolete compatibility headers like <varargs.h> are retained only to enforce migration. Overall, gcc/ginclude is the boundary layer where GCC publishes standardized headers and compatibility macros derived from the compiler’s own type system, builtins, and target properties, distinct from front-end parsing or backend code generation modules.
